newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs stay soft on refinery maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs stay soft on refinery maintenance.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates from the key Middle East region remained soft on Thursday due to upcoming refinery maintenance in Japan and South Korea and Moslem holidays, brokers said.
Rates to Japan and South Korea were around W50, at a par with Singapore and western destinations, and up to 15 points lower than recent levels.
"There are a lot of Japanese re-lets and with refinery maintenance rates are likely to stay low for a while longer," one broker said.
West Africa/U.S. VLCCs were stable at W67.5/70, while West Africa/eastward activity was quiet because of the looming refinery maintenance programme.

Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) from West Africa and northern Europe to the U.S. were also steady at W97.5, while cross-Med they edged up to W97.5 on good activity both locally and in the West African market, brokers said.

Cross-Med 80,000 tonne (Aframax) cargoes also saw fair activity with the rate steady at about W125, or up to 10 points higher for prompt positions. Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes were unchanged at W100, brokers added.
An Italian broker described the Med fuel oil tanker market as "very depressed," with 25,000 tonnes at W175, down some 20 points, on plentiful tonnage, while inter-UKC was stable at W180.

Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonne crude cargoes remained at around a firm W220/225 where they have been since the end of March and some 70 points above the average for last year, according to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc.
